naslov: How to Watch the NBA in Australia 2026-27 | ESPN on Disney+
tekst:
The 2026-27 NBA season tips off live on ESPN at 6am AEDT on Wednesday, 21 October, with a blockbuster opening-day triple-header headlined by LeBron James' Philadelphia 76ers debut against the champion New York Knicks. ESPN is included in every Disney+ plan, so the start of what shapes as one of the most open title races in years -- after an offseason of unprecedented superstar movement -- is only a few taps away.
Here's everything you need to know about how to watch the NBA in Australia this season: where every game is broadcast, what it costs, the opening week schedule in AEDT, and when to catch the nine Australians on NBA rosters.
How to watch the NBA in Australia
• ESPN on Disney+ -- an average of seven live NBA games every week, plus the NBA Boxing Day marathon, All-Star Weekend, the playoffs and the NBA Finals.
• ESPN and ESPN2 on Kayo Sports, Foxtel and Fetch TV -- the same ESPN coverage if you already subscribe to one of these.
• Prime Video -- selected games, mostly on Saturday mornings in Australia, plus the NBA Cup and the Play-In Tournament.
• NBA League Pass 
Watch the NBA on ESPN on Disney+
ESPN is Australia's home court for the NBA, and Disney+ is the simplest to get it. ESPN and ESPN2 broadcast an average of seven live NBA games every week of the regular season, along with the NBA Boxing Day marathon, NBA All-Star Weekend, the NBA Playoffs and the NBA Finals.
The coverage goes beyond the games, too. Nothing But Net brings an Australian perspective to the league's biggest stories, alongside ESPN favourites NBA Today, SportsCenter, First Take and Inside the NBA. Check ESPN's weekly "How to watch this week's NBA on Disney+" guide for each week's live games.

ESPN and ESPN2 are available on Disney+, Kayo Sports, Foxtel and Fetch TV. Every other game is live on NBA League Pass.
Opening week storylines
Celtics at Pistons (Wed 6am, ESPN): Boston's new era begins with Paul George alongside Jayson Tatum, against Cade Cunningham and a rising Detroit side. The two teams finished with the East's best two records last season.
76ers at Knicks (Wed 10am, ESPN): The headline act. The Knicks raise their first championship banner since 1973 and start their title defence against a new-look Philadelphia, where LeBron James joins Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown. The Knicks bring back their full starting five of Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges.
Thunder at Spurs (Wed 12:30pm, ESPN): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander against Victor Wembanyama, in a rematch of last season's Western Conference finals, which the Spurs won in seven.
Timberwolves at Heat (Thu 10:30am): Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami debut, and LaMelo Ball's first game for Minnesota.
Warriors at Lakers (Thu 1pm, ESPN): Luka Dončić and the Lakers begin life without LeBron against Steph Curry.
Cavaliers at 76ers (Fri 10am): LeBron's Philadelphia home debut against Donovan Mitchell, with Boomers guard Tyrese Proctor in Cleveland's rotation.
Nuggets at Thunder (Fri 12:30pm): Two-time reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander against three-time MVP Nikola Jokić.
Wizards at Bulls (Sun 25 Oct, 11am, ESPN2): Josh Giddey's first ESPN game of the season, against a Washington side entering a new era with Trae Young, Anthony Davis and No. 1 draft pick AJ Dybantsa.
The rest of the week: Pistons at 76ers (Mon, ESPN2), Warriors at Nuggets (Tue, ESPN on Disney+), then a Wednesday ESPN2 doubleheader of Pistons at Knicks and Trail Blazers at Lakers.

Dyson Daniels and Josh Giddey remain the faces of Australian basketball in the NBA, each on matching four-year, US$100 million deals -- Daniels as one of the league's premier young guards, Giddey as one of its most versatile playmakers. Giddey's Bulls have the most Australia-friendly schedule of any team, with the vast majority of their games landing in the 10am-2pm window, and Aussie fans get their first look on ESPN2 on Sunday, 25 October against the Wizards.
